question: Can a correctness detector generalize beyond its training benchmark by reading both how an LLM residual-stream trajectory moves and a deliberately bottlenecked account of where its answer states lie, without reverting to the lexical shortcuts of static activation probes?

key_findings.claim: Static residual states contain more immediately decodable correctness signal than layer displacements, but they also expose substantially more answer wording; this motivates restoring only restricted location information beside motion.
key_findings.evidence: On ARC-Challenge, a mid-layer static linear probe reaches 68.6% selection accuracy versus 62.2% for the displacement reader. Yet held-out reconstruction/retrieval of answer wording is much higher from the raw last-token state (R2 0.086; retrieval ratio 2.26) or answer-pooled state (0.191; 3.13) than from learned motion (0.007; 1.01), direction (0.009; 1.32), or quantized region (-0.003; 1.05) embeddings.

key_findings.claim: Combining motion, continuous normalized direction, and a discrete region code gives broad cross-benchmark reasoning-error transfer rather than an in-domain-only probe gain.
key_findings.evidence: Across six single-donor training benchmarks and eight reasoning targets on Llama-3.1-8B, the full detector is best among trained readers in 47 of 48 cells. Its out-of-distribution mean exceeds a validation-selected linear probe by 10-21 points and the prior motion-only TaT reader by 7-12 points; for the ARC-Challenge donor, OOD accuracy is 75.2 versus 64.1 for the probe and 63.2 for motion.

key_findings.claim: A detector trained only on multiple-choice reasoning transfers zero-shot to two structurally different kinds of factual error, although base-model likelihood remains stronger on minimal-edit completion sets.
key_findings.evidence: Averaged over the three strongest reasoning donors, selection accuracy on FACTOR-wiki/news/expert and VitaminC is 51.9/58.2/69.5/67.1 for the full detector, versus 39.4/44.9/50.8/57.6 for motion and 30.0/31.2/55.5/62.3 for the probe. Frozen answer likelihood scores the FACTOR sets at 57.9/72.3/74.6, but the detector narrowly leads on evidence-conditioned VitaminC, 67.1 versus 65.1.

key_findings.claim: The two location streams are complementary to motion and to each other, but the learned fixed fusion leaves substantial per-item value unused.
key_findings.evidence: From an ARC-Challenge donor, adding direction to motion improves the eight reasoning targets by 3-20 points and adding region improves seven targets by 4-15 points; using both is best in every ablation row. In a separately trained late-fusion diagnostic, all three streams uniquely solve items missed by the other two, while an oracle that trusts any correct stream beats trained fusion by 3-21 points: for FACTOR-expert, direction alone is 69.5, fusion 57.2, and oracle 77.5; for VitaminC they are 53.1, 65.0, and 86.2.

key_findings.claim: Hard vector quantization preserves a coarse, cross-domain correctness coordinate, but its strength depends sharply on how much location signal the underlying model contains.
key_findings.evidence: A code-only majority vote from the 128-entry ARC-Challenge codebook beats the per-set base rate on ARC-Challenge (81.2 vs 75.0), StoryCloze (88.2 vs 50.0), and VitaminC (62.8 vs 54.4), but barely on FACTOR-expert (76.1 vs 75.0). Every code used by factual examples is also used by reasoning examples. Before quantization, a layer-14 state probe has AUC 0.92 on FACTOR-expert but only 0.61 on FACTOR-wiki, exposing a model-side ceiling.

key_findings.claim: Location is most useful in the middle third of the network for reasoning, whereas factual discrimination benefits from reading all depths.
key_findings.evidence: Retraining the full reader with controlled layer windows gives reasoning means of 63.7, 75.6, and 69.5 for early, middle, and late thirds. Six middle-third layers exceed all 32 layers on reasoning (75.6 vs 74.0), while all layers produce the best factual mean (63.7 vs 61.3 for the middle third), largely through late factual signal.

key_findings.claim: The gain is not explained by parameter count, normalization alone, answer-length leakage, or a single model family.
key_findings.evidence: The location streams add 0.314M parameters, 6.7% of the motion LSTM; a 25.7M-parameter width-512 motion reader still trails the 5.1M full reader by about ten reasoning points. Normalizing the motion displacements does not reproduce the gain, and every retained benchmark is below chance for a shortest-answer rule. On Qwen2.5-14B and Qwen3-30B-A3B, the full reader exceeds the stronger baseline by 8-14 reasoning points and 11-16 factual points, with one losing cell in the detailed reasoning grid.

key_findings.claim: The main Llama reasoning result is stable over detector-training seeds, but many explanatory and cross-model analyses remain single-seed.
key_findings.evidence: Across three seeds, the per-donor reasoning means have standard deviations from 0.1 to 1.0 points and the cross-donor mean is 73.1+/-0.4, far below the baseline gap. The factual table, component ablation, region analysis, late-fusion diagnostic, width and normalization controls, and both Qwen replications are explicitly labeled single-seed.

method.core_idea: Keep the prior Truth-as-a-Trajectory displacement reader unchanged, then add two tightly restricted views of state location: a coarse vector-quantized region at the final answer token and a fine continuous direction across answer tokens and six fixed middle-to-late depths.
method.mechanism: For every question-candidate pair, a frozen base model produces one residual-state tensor over tokens and layers. A two-layer bidirectional LSTM reads all layerwise displacements. Both location readers discard residual magnitude, question tokens, and all but six fixed depths after applying a depth-shared projection to unit-normalized states. The region branch encodes the final answer token and hard-assigns it to one of 128 EMA-updated codebook entries using a straight-through estimator and commitment loss. The direction branch applies a shared MLP to continuous projected directions and joins final-token and answer-span means. Concatenated stream embeddings are trained with a pairwise objective, and the highest candidate score is selected.
assumptions: Every evaluation item supplies a finite candidate set with exactly one labeled correct answer; the detector is a ranker, not an absolute verifier.
A full residual-stream forward pass is available for every candidate, and the frozen model already encodes some correctness information in its states or displacements.
Unit direction retains task-general state location while magnitude and most tokens/layers are more likely to carry scale or wording confounds.
A single labeled donor benchmark contains enough positive and negative candidates to train a model-specific detector that transfers to new benchmarks.
The fixed six-depth window is comparable across 32- and 48-layer base models, despite different model families and residual widths.
Selection accuracy is a meaningful measure of error detection even though it does not test calibration or standalone correctness judgments.

techniques.role: Reads what each transformer layer changes while attenuating persistent token content.
Removes depth-dependent residual magnitude before sharing projections across layers.
Passes only a discrete activation-space region so the classifier cannot recover fine coordinates.
Keeps fine orientation at separate depths while omitting question tokens and most of the layer stack.
Combines the settled final-token state with the mean path across answer tokens.
Trains on one reasoning source at a time and measures all off-diagonal benchmark cells as zero-shot transfer.
Quantifies lexical information recoverable from each learned embedding and compares it with raw states.
Exposes which items each stream can solve alone and upper-bounds gains from item-adaptive routing.

evaluations.setting: Llama-3.1-8B; six reasoning donors, eight reasoning targets
evaluations.metric: Candidate selection accuracy, ID and OOD means
evaluations.result: Full reader wins 47/48 trained-reader cells; OOD gains are 10-21 points over the probe and 7-12 over motion
evaluations.baseline: Validation-selected static linear probe and Truth-as-a-Trajectory motion-only bi-LSTM

evaluations.setting: Reasoning-trained Llama detectors on FACTOR-wiki/news/expert and VitaminC
evaluations.result: Full reader averages 51.9/58.2/69.5/67.1 and beats both trained baselines on all four targets
evaluations.baseline: Probe 30.0/31.2/55.5/62.3; motion 39.4/44.9/50.8/57.6; frozen likelihood remains stronger on FACTOR

evaluations.metric: Selection accuracy on eight reasoning targets
evaluations.result: Direction and region each improve motion; both together are best in all eight rows, reaching 74.7 on ARC-C and 96.9 on StoryCloze

evaluations.setting: Late-fusion stream diagnostic on ARC-C, StoryCloze, FACTOR-expert, VitaminC
evaluations.metric: Per-stream, fused, and per-item-oracle selection accuracy
evaluations.result: Every stream uniquely recovers items; oracle gains over fusion range from 3 to 21 points
evaluations.baseline: Best single stream and learned fixed fusion

evaluations.setting: Region-code analysis from one ARC-Challenge-trained 128-entry codebook
evaluations.metric: Codes used and code-only majority-vote correctness
evaluations.result: Code-only prediction beats base rate on all four inspected datasets; factual code support is a subset of reasoning code support
evaluations.baseline: Dataset correctness base rate and raw-state AUC

evaluations.result: Middle third is best for reasoning at 75.6; all layers are best for factual transfer at 63.7
evaluations.baseline: Early third 63.7/52.5, late third 69.5/57.3, fixed paper window 72.6/60.3

evaluations.setting: Qwen2.5-14B dense and Qwen3-30B-A3B MoE, three donors
evaluations.metric: Cross-donor reasoning and factual selection means
evaluations.result: Full reader scores 82.3/63.6 and 82.2/62.2, beating the stronger trained baseline by 8-14 and 11-16 points
evaluations.baseline: Per-model better of probe and motion

evaluations.setting: Width, normalization, lexical-confound, and seed controls
evaluations.metric: Accuracy, parameter count, wording reconstruction/retrieval, and standard deviation
evaluations.result: Added capacity and displacement normalization do not close the gap; learned streams reveal much less wording than raw states; main reasoning mean is 73.1+/-0.4 across seeds
evaluations.baseline: Up to width-512 motion reader, raw/normalized motion, raw residual state, and alternate seeds

limitations: Author-stated: the detector is evaluated only by selecting among supplied candidates and is never asked whether one standalone answer is correct.
Author-stated: it requires residual-stream access, one forward pass per candidate, a labeled donor benchmark, and separate training for every base model.
Author-stated: performance is bounded by correctness information already present in the model; raw-state AUC varies from 0.61 to 0.92 across two FACTOR domains.
Author-stated: direction normalization discards magnitude that may contain correctness signal, and a separate magnitude channel remains untested.
Author-stated: a per-item oracle exceeds learned fusion by 3-21 points, showing the three readings are not yet combined effectively.

Reviewer-identified: most mechanistic ablations, factual results, region-code claims, and cross-model replications use one detector-training seed, and FACTOR-expert has only 236 items with very small held-out probe splits.

Reviewer-identified: all donors are answer-selection benchmarks; there is no evaluation on free-form generated chains, intermediate-step errors, self-correction, adversarially constructed candidates, or correctness after distribution shift in prompting style.

Reviewer-identified: low wording reconstruction does not prove the streams encode causal correctness rather than a different benchmark shortcut; the work performs no activation intervention or counterfactual steering.
Reviewer-identified: hard region codes are associated with correctness by majority vote but are not semantically identified, stable across models, or shown causally necessary.
Reviewer-identified: scoring every candidate with a separate full forward pass can be expensive when candidate sets are large and does not apply directly when alternatives are unavailable.
Reviewer-identified: selection accuracy does not establish calibration, threshold portability, abstention quality, or error costs for deployment.
Reviewer-identified: only three open base-model families are tested, without instruction-tuned, chain-of-thought, closed, multilingual, or domain-specialized models.
failure_modes: If the base model's states do not separate valid from invalid candidates, no reader can recover the missing correctness signal.
A detector can rank one supplied option correctly while assigning unusable absolute scores, so it may fail as a standalone verifier or abstention mechanism.
Candidate formatting, tokenization, answer length, or authorship can provide shortcuts not captured by the reported shortest-answer and wording audits.
A fixed six-layer window can miss factual or architecture-specific signal concentrated near the output, as the all-layer factual result already indicates.
The VQ codebook can collapse or leave entries unused without data seeding, EMA updates, reseeding, and commitment loss; a collapsed region branch contributes little.
Hard quantization can merge correct and incorrect states in the same region, while the continuous direction branch can retain task-specific fine detail and overfit.
A donor that transfers weakly on reasoning also transfers weakly to factual sets, making donor selection a hidden dependency.
Fixed concatenation can trust the wrong stream on an item even when another stream is correct, particularly on FACTOR-expert and VitaminC.
Model updates, quantization, inaccessible residual streams, or a changed tokenizer require feature re-extraction and likely detector retraining.
The method's compute grows linearly with candidate count because each option requires its own forward pass.
reusable_insights: Separate trajectory motion from state location, then bottleneck location at multiple resolutions instead of choosing between raw probes and displacement-only readers.
Audit a verifier representation for reconstructable wording and answer retrieval, not just downstream accuracy, before interpreting it as a reasoning signal.
Use both a coarse code and a continuous direction: quantization aids invariance while direction recovers within-region distinctions.
Choose residual depths by the kind of judgment required; reasoning and factual verification can prefer different layer bands.
Measure per-item stream overlap and an oracle bound before adding more encoder capacity; a routing problem can masquerade as a representation problem.
Exclude evaluation sets solvable by label-independent heuristics and report the heuristic beside chance.
A small labeled donor can be useful if the detector reads a cross-task model invariant, but donor robustness must itself be evaluated across sources.
open_questions: Can the three streams yield a calibrated absolute correctness score for a single generated answer or intermediate reasoning step?
What item-adaptive gate can close the large oracle gap without learning new dataset shortcuts?
Does a separate, tightly controlled magnitude channel add genuine signal beyond direction and region?
Are region codes stable or alignable across base models, checkpoints, languages, and prompt formats?
Do causal interventions along learned directions or between code regions change correctness rather than only correlate with it?
Can activations from one shared generation pass score multiple sampled answers, reducing the one-forward-pass-per-candidate cost?
How does the detector behave against adversarial wrong answers matched for fluency, length, semantics, and model likelihood?
Would training directly on factual verification, math proofs, or generated chains improve transfer or destroy the invariant found from reasoning donors?

competitive_landscape.title: Truth as a Trajectory: What Internal Representations Reveal About Large Language Model Reasoning
competitive_landscape.difference: Truth as a Trajectory introduces the all-token, all-layer displacement bi-LSTM and argues that motion transfers better than static activations because it attenuates lexical content. The present paper explicitly leaves that reader unchanged and adds restricted state-location streams, recovering signal that displacement discards while preserving most of its transfer advantage.

competitive_landscape.title: The Geometry of Truth: Emergent Linear Structure in Large Language Model Representations of True/False Datasets
competitive_landscape.difference: Marks and Tegmark identify linear truth directions in static hidden states, test cross-dataset transfer, and provide causal activation interventions on true/false statements. This paper focuses on multi-candidate reasoning validity, combines depthwise motion with normalized multi-depth location, and audits wording leakage, but does not establish causal control.

competitive_landscape.title: The Geometry of Reasoning: Flowing Logics in Representation Space
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhou et al. use controlled natural-deduction propositions to model reasoning as semantic-invariant flows with position, velocity, and curvature, emphasizing theory and explicit logical segments. The current method treats transformer depth as a trajectory over candidate answers, learns a correctness selector across broad benchmarks, and uses region/direction bottlenecks rather than segmented proof-flow geometry.

competitive_landscape.title: Reasoning Models Know When They're Right: Probing Hidden States for Self-Verification
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhang et al. probe hidden states of reasoning models for intermediate-answer correctness and use calibrated scores for early exit, saving 24% of tokens. This paper targets frozen base models and cross-benchmark candidate selection, reads an entire layer trajectory, and tests factual transfer; it does not verify online reasoning steps or reduce generation length.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: correctness is legible in separable aspects of a residual trajectory—motion, a coarse region, and a fine direction—and restoring the latter two yields transferable reasoning and factual error detection with little lexical information. The displacement reader is explicitly inherited unchanged from the authors' prior Truth-as-a-Trajectory work, while static truth directions, cross-dataset probes, geometric reasoning flows, and hidden-state self-verification all predate this paper. Reviewer inference: the defensible new contribution is the particular dual-resolution location restoration—hard VQ region plus normalized multi-depth direction—integrated with TaT and subjected to cross-donor, factual, depth, capacity, normalization, and wording audits. The work supports a robust candidate-ranking representation; it does not yet establish an abstract, calibrated, causal notion of correctness or a verifier for unconstrained generated reasoning.
reviewer_notes: All 19 local PDF pages, including supplementary controls and full Qwen grids, were read. Quantitative claims distinguish three-seed main Llama rows from single-seed factual, ablation, region, and cross-model analyses. Primary arXiv records were used for direct comparisons. 'Correctness coordinate' is treated as an empirical ranking signal, not a causal semantic interpretation.
